decision: measured the shipped abs/av.glitch.pd before changing it
why: the report was white screen and no reaction, which needs reproducing not guessing
result: old chain emitted a texture-less gemlist and sent pix_roll its axis on the wrong inlet

decision: built a headless GEM render probe and measured frames instead of reading the patch
why: two attempted fixes had failed on the same assumption, so the observation method had to change
result: turned a guess loop into a measurement loop

decision: fixed the capture: pix_write needs color_format 4
why: every frame came back red-tinted, which looked like a render bug and was a grab bug
result: pix_write grabs 3 bytes per pixel from a 4 byte buffer by default

decision: worked out that GEM's projection is a fixed 4x4 world
why: the video was stretched and letterboxed, and both 4x3 and 1.6875x3 failed
result: a 4x4 quad in a 288x512 window fills it at the video's own aspect

decision: found the sweep was pinned at zero
why: the whole mosh was inert, which read as the video not reacting to audio
evidence: pd log, cycle_out 0 on every tick
result: Pd [%] truncates to int, so a float phase wraps to 0

decision: rewrote the control block as a latched 40 Hz poll
why: chained arithmetic only fires from its left inlet, so depth and amount were computed once at load
evidence: pd log, amount_clip printed once for a whole run
result: ordering is explicit now and every derived value settles within a tick

decision: tested pix_delay, pix_tIIR, pix_motionblur and pix_roll as the stale-frame source
why: three of the four emitted no texture, which is the white screen
result: pix_delay dropped; pix_motionblur is the one that is already a P-frame

decision: chose pix_motionblur then pix_roll as the shipped chain
why: blur alone was too subtle and roll alone was a plain scroll; together they melt and drag
evidence: vs clean baseline 47.0 at mod-2 90 versus 8.8 for blur alone
result: abs/av.glitch.pd

decision: verified idle is an exact passthrough
why: the ask was explicit that holds hard left must leave the video alone
evidence: vs clean baseline 0.0 with every bus at 0
result: idle structure is preserved

decision: wrote a real ffmpeg datamosh by dropping I-frames from the elementary stream
why: datamosh like in ffmpeg should be checkable against the real thing, not only a reconstruction
result: av/mosh_ref.mp4 melts visibly at frame 90

decision: ran the real abstraction with the real bus names
why: end to end rather than through the harness
result: idle white_frac 0.0023, active temporal_mad 46.1 against idle 35.2

decision: loaded the whole _LIRA-8.pd headless
why: the abstraction only ships if the app that instantiates it still starts
result: no object errors; the one audio warning predates this change

decision: identified the effect the user linked by pulling the video section and reading its own transcript
why: guessing at a named effect wastes a build; the tutorial names its own operators
evidence: yt-dlp section at 1052s, subtitle frequency: feedback 64, displace 33, optical flow 8
result: the effect is a feedback buffer whose stored motion is re-applied every frame through a displacement map

decision: checked whether GEM can carry a custom shader before committing to it
why: GEM was the user's first choice and the answer decides the whole approach
evidence: GEM ships glsl, glsl_fragment, glsl_vertex, glsl_program and 20 shader examples
result: GLSL compiles and links on this machine, so the look is not blocked by capability

decision: found the working chain order by rendering candidates instead of reading the help patches
why: the help patches ship unwired examples and the ones that are wired are nested three deep
evidence: pd render of three chain orders, only one produced a picture
result: pix_texture then rectangle then glsl_program; a shader shades geometry so the quad comes first

decision: found that GEM's glsl abstraction cannot hold dynamic uniforms
why: a shader whose values cannot move is useless for an audio-reactive effect
evidence: pd log, one vertex-stage error per uniform message; glsl_program print lists the uniforms it did link
result: dead end without either patching GEM or using the raw module objects

decision: found the raw glsl_vertex and glsl_fragment objects never report module ids
why: that is what glsl_program must link, so the clean route cannot be wired from Pd
evidence: pd log, glsl_program reports can't link zero shaders with relative and absolute shader paths
result: GEM shader route parked; abs/shader/mosh.frag kept with its status in the header

decision: checked whether Pd can speak OSC without installing anything
why: the TouchDesigner question is mostly a transport question, and an external dependency would be the hard part
evidence: oscformat and oscparse round trip in /tmp/osctest.pd
result: Pd vanilla ships oscformat, oscparse, netsend and netreceive, so the link needs no externals

decision: built and verified abs/av.osc.pd against the existing round-trip test
why: the test already existed and had nothing to point at
result: PASS: bus to OSC and OSC to bus both verified on 127.0.0.1 ports 9121 and 9122

decision: wired av.osc into _LIRA-8.pd
why: the bridge is only useful if the instrument carries it
result: app still loads headless; no object errors

decision: checked whether TouchDesigner is installed to run the other end
why: the whole point of the bridge is the far side
result: TouchDesigner is not on this machine and has to be installed before the bridge has anything to talk to

decision: dropped GEM and rebuilt the bridge to carry every bus, not a hand-picked few
why: the user asked for every output and a hand-kept list drifts the moment a control is added
result: 59 buses, and a new control shows up on the next run

decision: worked out the two naming families in the patch so the live value is the one mirrored
why: each control has both an s- and an r- bus and picking wrong mirrors a dead value
result: 19 buses are live readouts the engine pushes so they are read-only; 40 are writable controls

decision: found the widgets publish label and label_pos on the same buses
why: the full app filled the console with oscformat errors the isolated test never saw
evidence: pd log, five oscformat errors per load
result: added [route float] in front of every sender; [t f] filters but prints an error each time

decision: fixed the test's own OSC codec, which was padding a 4-aligned string with nothing
why: a 12 character address was not null-terminated so Pd's oscparse called it malformed
evidence: pd log, malformed type string; /lira/mod-12 came back with no value
result: both the encoder and the parser now add a whole null word after a 4-aligned string

decision: listened on the OSC port while the real instrument ran
why: the unit test only proves the abstraction, not that the app carries it
result: 49 addresses arrived, including /lira/cpu ten times as the meter ticked

decision: found the datamosh project is a clone with a ready Datamoshing.tox
why: the bridge needs a far end and the user pointed at this repo
result: the component was already available, so no network had to be built from scratch

decision: read the component with the app's own toeexpand instead of guessing at its parameters
why: the tox is encrypted and unreadable, but TouchDesigner ships expand and collapse tools
result: recovered the full parameter list and the internal network as text

decision: found the component is a recursive loop with only one way out
why: the melt accumulates forever, so the picture freezes instead of recovering
evidence: pixel shader and feedback1.parm, top is glslmulti
result: Offsetbymotionvector is the melt strength and Feedbackreset is the only reset

decision: wrote the wiring as a Textport script rather than a rebuilt toe
why: the script sets expressions through the API, so nothing about TouchDesigner's file format has to be guessed
result: one paste does the whole TD side and prints its own evidence

decision: stopped driving the TouchDesigner GUI after four attempts
why: the window lives on another Space, its accessibility surface keeps dropping, and the user was typing in a browser
evidence: container refusal, menu press reported unverifiable with no pane opening
result: handed back the one paste instead of taking over the screen
